newsitem.title: ROMANIA: DAEWOO SECURITIES OPENS ROMANIA BANK.
newsitem.headline: DAEWOO SECURITIES OPENS ROMANIA BANK.

text.p: South Korea's Daewoo Securities has opened a fully licensed bank in Romania in a bid to develop businesses and strenghten its position in the Balkan country, a senior bank executive said on Wednesday.

"The plans for our bank should be seen in the context of the Daewoo Group's overall projects in Romania, which include investment in automotive industry, shipbuilding and other manufacturing sectors," George Vasile, director of the new Daewwo Bank (Romania) SA, said during the opening ceremony.
The bank has a starting capital of 75 billion lei, the largest among the foreign banks operating in Romania, he said.
Daewoo Securities hold 89.9 percent, South Korea's KorAm Bank has 10 percent and four Romanian individuals take the rest of the shares.
"We are willing to take part in the capital market to secure market occupancy and exploration of new opportunities," Vasile said.

Daewoo already is a strong presence in Romania, where Daewoo Heavy Industries tops the list of foreign companies investing in Romania. The group already invested some $156 million in a joint venture with the Craiova-based Automobile Craiova car maker and spent $53 million to buy a controlling stake in the Black Sea shipyard of Mangalia.

The new bank's businesses would initially rely on Daewoo's activities in Romania, Vasile said. Eventually, its businesses would expand from trade, corporate financing and foreign exchange deals to credits for the population and issuing credit cards, he said.
The bank's future plans also included the opening of four branches across Romania, Vasile added.
Romania now has some 40 commercial banks, of which 10 are branches of foreign banks. ($=7,097)
